dedupe_keys.name: global inventory of groundwater use for irrigation siebert et al 2010

description: This 2010 article in Hydrology and Earth System Sciences presents a global inventory of the extent of areas irrigated with groundwater, surface water or non-conventional sources, with the related consumptive water use, for 15,038 national and sub-national administrative units. Irrigated areas came from census-based statistics of international and national organisations, and a global model simulated consumptive irrigation water use by source. The paper estimates about 301 million ha equipped for irrigation, 38% of it with groundwater, and consumptive groundwater use for irrigation of 545 km3 a year, 43% of the total, with India, China and the USA having the largest groundwater-irrigated areas. Coverage is global at national and sub-national level. Access is free as an open access article with a supplement of 7,489 KB under the journal's CC BY 4.0 licence. Caveats: the authors note uncertainties in the statistics, the inventory is a 2010 snapshot, and the supplement contents were not checked. Simulation uses: groundwater and surface water demand for irrigation supply models and drought exposure of groundwater-dependent irrigation. Related records: the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas) and AQUASTAT (data-fao-aquastat-main-database).
